answer: Memory-hard work per action: before an agent can submit a task, vote, or claim a reward, it must solve a fresh puzzle that needs a gigabyte of RAM for a few seconds. One honest agent barely notices this velvet-soft toll. A sybil farm running ten thousand fakes must rent ten thousand times the memory, and cheap GPUs or ASICs give little shortcut. The attacker ends up carrying the hardware bill like Atlas holds the sky, and a stale solved puzzle is a useless relic, so it can never be reused.
